skillDispatch.when: Writing, modifying, refactoring, or reviewing implementation code.
Writing, changing, or reviewing tests and fixtures.
Writing or revising technical documentation and delivery notes.
Fixing defects, regressions, or verification failures at their root cause.
Diagnosing a bug, failing check, or unexpected behavior before proposing a fix.
Making any completion, readiness, or handoff claim.

rules.guidance: Keep root agent instructions as short mandatory pointers. Setup owns only marked baseline content; preserve repository-authored bytes outside setup markers and keep project-specific architecture and policy in repository-owned documents.
Fix root causes. Do not suppress diagnostics, weaken assertions, swallow errors, add timing hacks, or bypass a required check to produce a passing result.
Use fresh evidence from the current worktree before claiming work complete, fixed, passing, ready, committed, or delivered. A narrower check supports only the behavior it exercised.
Run the selected repository Verification before completion claims. Treat every failure as blocking and report the command plus its actionable diagnostic.

Do not edit verification configuration, tests, fixtures, golden files, or generated expectations merely to make a failure disappear. Change them only when the repository contract intentionally changes, and prove the new contract.
Activate every matching required skill before governed work. When one skill has distinct active-module triggers, retain and follow each trigger.
Write generated repository guidance, identifiers, headings, and examples in English. Preserve repository-authored language outside setup-owned markers.
Search repository files with local code-search tools. For external APIs and libraries, use current authoritative documentation; do not use web research to infer local repository behavior.

Use the repository's declared package manager and lockfile workflow. Add or upgrade a dependency only for a named job the existing stack cannot perform, and keep manifest and lockfile changes together.

Inspect repository status before staging or delivery. Preserve unrelated work, avoid destructive Git operations, and never commit, push, create branches, or open pull requests without explicit authority.

Never read, print, commit, or generate secrets. Keep credentials and environment-specific values in the repository's existing secure configuration boundary, and do not invent authentication, authorization, database, transport, or deployment policy.
